title: Measure powdered formula into a 4-ounce bottle: two unpacked scoops, each leveled against the tin's leveling bar
instruction: Measure the formula into this bottle.
context: Childcare workers and nannies (O*NET 39-9011; 1.01 million jobs, BLS 2025), home health aides and parents measure powdered infant formula into bottles many times a day. US standard formulas are mixed at one unpacked, level scoop of powder per 2 fl oz of water (Similac's preparation directions), so the 4 fl oz of water already in this bottle takes exactly two level scoops. A scoop dipped into the powder comes out heaped, and a heaped scoop holds about 29% more powder than a level one; pressing the powder down adds more. The CDC's formula guidance says to use the exact amounts on the container because adding too much or too little formula can make a baby sick, and powder stirred into water cannot be taken back out. The skill is the physical measuring: dig the scoop through the powder, draw it up against the tin's leveling bar so the heap falls back in, tip it into the bottle's neck, twice, without packing or spilling; capping and shaking come after and are not part of this task.
setup: Positions are in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, with x forward, y to the robot's left and the table top at z 0. All objects are fixed except the scoop. A white steel formula tin, 14.6 cm across and 10 cm tall with a plain pale-blue label band, lid off, stands with its axis at x 31, y 11; it holds 700 g of pale cream powder (0.50 g/mL loose) whose top is about 0.65 cm below the rim. A rigid gray leveling bar 1 cm wide and 0.4 cm thick is fixed across the opening along x, its center line at y 12.5, its underside at the rim (10 cm). A clear 270 mL wide-neck plastic bottle, 6 cm across and 11.5 cm tall to the top of its neck (5 cm opening), stands in a gray holder ring 9 cm across at x 40, y -3; it holds 120 mL (4 fl oz) of water with the 120 mL line marked. A dark-blue plastic scoop (45 g with a weighted handle) lies on a white scoop stand at x 23, y -12.5: its round handle, 2.5 cm across and 7 cm long, runs along y with its center at y -12.5, 8 cm up, resting on a post 1.6 cm wide; a neck runs down from the handle's +y end to a round bowl 3.9 cm across outside (3.6 cm inside, 1.75 cm deep, 17.8 mL) whose center is at y -4.75, resting on a 3.5 cm square pad 2.2 cm tall. A level scoop of this powder weighs 8.9 g, close to the 8.6 to 8.8 g on US labels.
scoring: A correct feed is two level scoops, 17.8 g, since the label mixes one level scoop per 2 fl oz and the bottle holds 4 fl oz. The powder in the bottle is weighed at the end, held for 1 s. 1.0: 16.6 to 19.1 g in the bottle, every scoop drawn along the leveling bar, under 1 g spilled, and the scoop let go (no hand touching it) and at rest on the table or back on its stand, since the hand is needed next to cap the bottle and a scoop left in the tin or across the bottle is in the way. 0.5: the same dose, but the scoop is still held, moving, off the table, in the tin or across the bottle, or 1 g or more is spilled: the feed is right, but the job is not finished cleanly. 0.25: one level scoop, 8.3 to 9.5 g: half the feed is measured right, and a second scoop can still finish it. 0: any scoop that reached the bottle without being drawn along the bar (heaped or only tipped, so not level), the bottle ever holding over 19.1 g (powder cannot come back out of water), any other amount, or doing nothing. The window is 7%, the error of a scoop leveled 1 mm short of the bar. A real trial weighs the bottle on a 0.1 g scale before and after, weighs any powder brushed off the table, and checks on video that each scoop was drawn along the bar.
reset_notes: Pour out the bottle and refill it with 120 mL of water; top the tin back up to 700 g and smooth the surface; lay the scoop back on its stand, clean and dry. Powder in the bottle is consumed. Before the first trial with a new tin or lot, recalibrate the gram windows from 10 weighed level scoops (see the README's real-world build).
fidelity: The powder is a scored bulk model, not particles: densities (loose 0.50 g/mL, packed 0.64), heaps at a 42 degree angle of repose, dips, the strike-off under the bar, pours and spills move grams from the poses each step. The powder has no weight or collision, so a tipped scoop would shed its heap exactly; the scorer therefore requires the bar. The heap is drawn in the powder's own cream color, inside the bowl's mouth; stirring the bottle is not modeled.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0 (2,400 steps); demo: 1.0 (1,289 steps). Mistake variants in the sim: do nothing 0, two heaped scoops 0, one heaped and one level 0 (caught by the strike-off rule), one level scoop 0.25, three level scoops 0.
